clinical_recommendation: Diagnostic variant for PKU. Requires lifelong phenylalanine-restricted diet, metabolic monitoring, and consideration of sapropterin (BH4) therapy if responsive.
Lower warfarin dose requirement if anticoagulation ever needed. Use a validated pharmacogenomic dosing algorithm.
Combine with VKORC1 result for warfarin dosing algorithm; reduced clearance increases bleeding/toxicity risk at standard doses.
Most common East Asian founder variant for Wilson disease. Requires copper chelation therapy (e.g. penicillamine, trientine) or zinc therapy, with lifelong monitoring.
Reduced clopidogrel activation - consider alternative antiplatelet if PCI indicated. Reduced voriconazole clearance risk.
Impairs LDL receptor binding, causing markedly elevated LDL-C from birth. Requires statin therapy +/- ezetimibe/PCSK9 inhibitors and cascade family screening.
Significantly increased risk of simvastatin-induced myopathy. Avoid high-dose simvastatin; prefer rosuvastatin or pravastatin for this FH patient.
G6PD deficiency is both the underlying diagnosis and the pharmacogenomic marker. Rasburicase is CONTRAINDICATED. Avoid oxidative-stress-inducing drugs and fava beans; counsel on hemolysis triggers.
Most common FMF-causing variant. First-line treatment is daily colchicine; homozygosity is associated with more severe phenotype and higher amyloidosis risk.
If colchicine-refractory and thiopurine therapy considered, elevated myelosuppression risk - CPIC recommends 30-70% of standard dose with monitoring.
Classic C282Y homozygosity - most common genetic cause of hereditary hemochromatosis in Northern Europeans. First-line treatment is therapeutic phlebotomy.
Reduced conversion of codeine/tramadol to active metabolites - reduced analgesia. Reduced tamoxifen activation to endoxifen if ever indicated.
Nonsense variant causing loss of MLH1 mismatch-repair function. Requires enhanced colorectal/endometrial cancer surveillance and cascade family testing.

CRITICAL pre-chemotherapy test: significantly elevated risk of severe/life-threatening fluoropyrimidine toxicity. CPIC recommends 50% dose reduction or alternative agent before starting adjuvant chemo for this patient's colorectal cancer.
Severe deficiency genotype. Associated with early-onset emphysema (especially with smoking) and liver disease. Consider augmentation therapy and smoking cessation counseling.
HIGH-RISK: confers high risk of abacavir hypersensitivity reaction. Abacavir is CONTRAINDICATED if antiretroviral therapy is ever needed - select alternative agent.
Standard clopidogrel dosing generally adequate; monitor SSRI response as levels may be subtherapeutic at standard dose.
